What is Ruby and what makes it unique?

Ruby is a dynamic, interpreted, object-oriented scripting language emphasizing programmer happiness and productivity.

Key uniqueness:
- **Everything is an object** — even numbers and nil
- **Blocks** — closure-like constructs passed to methods with `{ }` or `do...end`
- **Open classes** — you can add methods to any class, even built-ins
- **Only false and nil are falsy** — 0 and "" are truthy!

Ruby on Rails is the most famous framework.

```bash
ruby hello.rb
irb          # interactive REPL
gem install rails
bundle exec ruby hello.rb
```

What are the Ruby variable types and naming conventions?

```ruby
local_var   = 42           # local variable
@instance   = "instance"   # instance variable
@@class_var = "class"      # class variable
$global     = "global"     # global variable
CONSTANT    = 3.14159      # constant (uppercase)

# Numbers
n   = 42
big = 10 ** 100            # arbitrary precision Bignum
f   = 3.14
r   = 3/4r                 # Rational: (3/4)
c   = 2 + 3i               # Complex

# Truthiness rule (IMPORTANT!)
# Only false and nil are falsy — everything else is truthy!
if 0          # TRUTHY in Ruby (unlike C/Python!)
if ""         # TRUTHY in Ruby
if nil        # falsy
if false      # falsy

# Symbols (immutable, interned — like atoms in Elixir)
:hello
:world
:hello.to_s    # "hello"
"hello".to_sym # :hello

# String interpolation
name = "Alice"
puts "Hello, #{name}!"
puts "2 + 2 = #{2 + 2}"
```

How do arrays and hashes work in Ruby?

```ruby
# Array
arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
arr.push(6)          # arr << 6 also works
arr.pop              # remove last
arr.shift            # remove first
arr.unshift(0)       # prepend
arr.first(3)         # [1, 2, 3]
arr.last(2)          # [5, 6]
arr.length; arr.size; arr.count
arr.include?(3)
arr.flatten
arr.compact          # remove nils
arr.uniq             # remove duplicates
arr.sort; arr.sort_by { |x| -x }
arr.reverse
arr.min; arr.max; arr.sum

# Hash
h = { name: "Alice", age: 30 }    # symbol keys (preferred)
h = { "name" => "Alice" }         # string keys
h[:name]            # "Alice"
h[:city] = "NYC"
h.delete(:age)
h.keys; h.values
h.each { |k, v| puts "#{k}: #{v}" }
h.map { |k, v| [k, v.to_s] }.to_h
h.select { |k, v| v.is_a?(String) }
h.merge({ zip: "10001" })
h.fetch(:name, "default")

# Range
(1..10)          # inclusive
(1...10)         # exclusive
('a'..'z').to_a  # ["a", "b", ... "z"]
(1..10).select(&:odd?)
(1..10).reduce(:+)
```

How do Ruby classes and inheritance work?

```ruby
class Animal
  attr_accessor :name, :sound    # generates getter+setter
  attr_reader   :id              # getter only

  @@count = 0   # class variable

  def initialize(name, sound)
    @name = name
    @sound = sound
    @id = @@count += 1
  end

  def speak
    "#{@name} says #{@sound}"
  end

  def to_s
    "Animal(#{@name})"
  end

  def self.count     # class method
    @@count
  end
end

class Dog < Animal   # inheritance
  attr_reader :breed

  def initialize(name, breed)
    super(name, "Woof")  # call parent __init__
    @breed = breed
  end

  def speak
    super + "!"   # call parent method
  end

  def fetch
    "#{name} fetches!"
  end
end

rex = Dog.new("Rex", "Labrador")
puts rex.speak    # Rex says Woof!
puts rex.fetch    # Rex fetches!
puts Animal.count  # 1
```

How do modules and mixins work in Ruby?

```ruby
# Module as namespace
module MathUtils
  PI = 3.14159265

  def self.circle_area(r)
    PI * r * r
  end

  # Mixed-in method (available to includers)
  def square
    self * self
  end
end

# Open class — add methods to ANY class!
class Integer
  include MathUtils
end

5.square   # 25
MathUtils.circle_area(5)  # 78.54

# Enumerable mixin — gives you 50+ methods for free!
class NumberList
  include Enumerable

  def initialize(*nums) @nums = nums end
  def each(&block) @nums.each(&block) end  # only need to define each!
end

nl = NumberList.new(3, 1, 4, 1, 5)
nl.sort          # [1, 1, 3, 4, 5]
nl.min; nl.max   # 1, 5
nl.select(&:odd?)  # [3, 1, 1, 5]
nl.map { |n| n * 2 }
nl.include?(4)   # true
nl.count; nl.sum; nl.min_by { |n| -n }

# Comparable mixin
class Temperature
  include Comparable
  attr_reader :degrees
  def initialize(d) @degrees = d end
  def <=>(other) degrees <=> other.degrees end  # only need <=>
end

temps = [Temperature.new(30), Temperature.new(15)]
temps.sort.first.degrees   # 15
```

How does exception handling and file I/O work in Ruby?

```ruby
# begin/rescue/ensure/raise
begin
  result = 10 / 0
rescue ZeroDivisionError => e
  puts "Math error: #{e.message}"
rescue TypeError, ArgumentError => e
  puts "Error: #{e.message}"
rescue => e     # catch all StandardError
  puts "Error: #{e.message}"
  raise         # re-raise same exception
else
  puts "Success: #{result}"  # runs only if no exception
ensure
  puts "Always runs"
end

# raise
raise ArgumentError, "must be positive" unless x > 0
raise "Something went wrong"

# Custom exception
class AppError < StandardError
  attr_reader :code
  def initialize(msg, code = nil)
    super(msg)
    @code = code
  end
end

raise AppError.new("Not found", 404)

# File I/O
content = File.read("file.txt")
lines   = File.readlines("file.txt").map(&:chomp)

File.open("file.txt") do |f|
  f.each_line { |line| puts line }
end

File.write("out.txt", "Hello\n")
File.open("out.txt", "a") { |f| f.puts "Appended" }

# CSV
require 'csv'
CSV.foreach("data.csv", headers: true) do |row|
  puts row["name"]
end
```

How does Ruby metaprogramming work (method_missing, define_method, open classes)?

```ruby
# method_missing — intercept unknown method calls
class DynamicProxy
  def initialize(target) @target = target end

  def method_missing(name, *args, &block)
    if @target.respond_to?(name)
      @target.send(name, *args, &block)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(name, include_private = false)
    @target.respond_to?(name) || super
  end
end

# define_method — create methods dynamically
[:double, :triple].each do |op|
  define_method("#{op}_value") do |n|
    op == :double ? n * 2 : n * 3
  end
end

# send — call methods dynamically (even private)
"hello".send(:upcase)   # "HELLO"

# class_eval — add methods to class at runtime
class Person; end
Person.class_eval do
  def greet; "Hello!"; end
end

# Reflection
"hello".class                   # String
"hello".is_a?(String)           # true
"hello".respond_to?(:upcase)    # true
String.instance_methods(false)  # methods defined ONLY in String
String.ancestors                # [String, Comparable, Object, Kernel, BasicObject]

# Frozen objects
str = "hello".freeze
str << " world"   # FrozenError!
str.frozen?       # true
```
